This document outlines the equipment inspection I1, which must be performed on 
weekly bases as indicated by W1 in the title block.

This Redundancy Communications Module (RCM)
provides a path for a synchronizing message from 
the active to 
the backup unit which is used to synchronize
the two CPUs in a FIP single rack redundancy 
system. It 
also provides the path for the transfer of shared I/O
data between the two units. The physical connection
between units in a FIP single rack redundancy 
system can 
have up to 3 feet (0.9 meters) total of
interconnecting cable. The CPUs for FIP single rack
Redundancy systems can be either IC697CPX928

The first draft is initiated by eng. Mohamed Tawfeeq, tested by 
eng. Bahaa Abd El-Wahab, revised by MDEPC quality control eng. Adel El Nagga, accepted by 
general manager eng. Mohamed Elshreif, approved by eng. Ahmed Sawan head sector 
of Nubaria power station .

This document certified by eng. Samir Abd El Gillil

sections.text:
This Redundancy 
Communications Module (RCM) provides a path for a synchronizing message from the 
active to the backup unit which is used to synchronize the two CPUs in a FIP 
single rack redundancy system. It also provides the path for the transfer of 
shared I/O data between the two units. The physical connection between units in 
a FIP single rack redundancy system can have up to 3 feet (0.9 meters) total of 
interconnecting cable. The CPUs for FIP single rack.

Redundancy systems can be 
either IC697CPX928 or IC697CPX935.

The five green LEDs at the top of the module provide
status information. The top LED (BOARD OK) is ON
when power is applied, the board is configured, 
there were no 
diagnostic failures in the RCM, no diagnostic
failures when establishing communications (the 
link) with 
the other RCM, and no failures in communications
on the link.

The other LEDs (LOCAL READY, LOCAL ACTIVE,
REMOTE READY, and REMOTE ACTIVE) indicate the
control status of the Primary and Secondary units 
in a Hot Standby CPU Redundancy system.
A work permit must be issued

Features
Supports FIP Redundant system configurations.
Two Redundancy Communications Modules required
 per system (in redundancy rack).
Single slot VME width module
Provides path for shared I/O and synchronizing
 message between Primary and Secondary MFCs.
High Speed Parallel Bus Expansion Interface.
Five LED indicators for board and system status.
Pushbutton switch for manual switch from active to
 backup unit.
Functions
This Redundancy 
Communications Module (RCM) provides a path for a synchronizing message from the 
active to the backup unit which is used to synchronize the two CPUs in a FIP 
single rack redundancy system. It also provides the path for the transfer of 
shared I/O data between the two units. The physical connection between units in 
a FIP single rack redundancy system can have up to 3 feet (0.9 meters) total of 
interconnecting cable. The CPUs for FIP single rack.
Redundancy systems can be 
either IC697CPX928 or IC697CPX935.
Status Indications
The five green LEDs at the top of the module provide
status information. The top LED (BOARD OK) is ON
when power is applied, the board is configured, 
there were no 
diagnostic failures in the RCM, no diagnostic
failures when establishing communications (the 
link) with 
the other RCM, and no failures in communications
on the link.
The other LEDs (LOCAL READY, LOCAL ACTIVE,
REMOTE READY, and REMOTE ACTIVE) indicate the
control status of the Primary and Secondary units 
in a Hot Standby CPU Redundancy system.
Safety 
Precautions
A work permit must be issued
Maintenance staff should be 
 well trained and qualified.
Caution marks must be 
 hanged on the work place, safety rope around the work place.
Removing a module
 MFC power must be off when connecting or disconnecting the transceiver

and Equipment
